title: Seismic waves and Earth's interior

accuracy.evidence: Shadow zone limits (no direct P from 104° to 140°; S stopped by the liquid core, P refracted by it) match the USGS Earthquake Hazards 'Shadow zone' page. Oldham 1906 and 'paths curve because speed changes with depth' follow USGS 'The Interior of the Earth'. Jeffreys 1926 and Lehmann 1936 follow APS News (2023) and Lehmann's 'P′' paper. Radii (Earth 6,371 km, core 3,480 km, inner core 1,220 km) and crustal speeds (P about 6 km/s, S about 3.5 km/s) follow PREM. The lab gap uses d/3.5 − d/6, giving 12, 24 and 48 s at 100, 200 and 400 km, which matches the 8 km per second rule in the items.

misconceptions.evidence: Predictions and challenge tags target the documented slips for this topic: longitudinal and transverse swapped (step 1 predict, 'dir'), S waves crossing liquids (step 2 predict), a fixed S minus P gap (step 3 predict, 'lag'), the core known from drilling (step 5 predict, 'drill'), the whole core liquid or solid ('solid') and S arriving first ('order').

lab_distinct.evidence: Built on seismology's own mechanisms: P and S property sorting beside a compression spring and a shear spring, four pass-or-stop tests in solid rock and liquid, a draggable seismometer whose live trace shows the P and S arrivals and the S minus P gap against distance, a cut-through Earth where tapping the surface places stations and colours the 104° to 140° and beyond-140° zones, and clue-to-layer reasoning. It shares no mechanism with flag_quake.js (magnitude scales).

lab_teaches.evidence: Each idea is found by acting first: a card filed in the wrong bin is refused with the reason; an S wave sent into liquid is stopped with the rigidity explanation; dragging the station visibly pulls the S line away from the P line; stations past 104° lose their S path and stations in 104° to 140° get nothing; only then does the clue step ask what each pattern implies.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with tempting wrong options that the lab then disproves: 'Up and down, across the path' for a P wave (the P spring compresses along its length), 'Yes, just like a P wave' for S in liquid (test 4 stops it), 'stays the same' for the gap (the trace gap grows as the station moves), and 'From rock brought up from the core' (clue 1 shows the evidence is S waves).

challenge_feedback.evidence: slip() gives a specific message for each wrong tag: dir (the P wave pushes along the path), solid (outer core liquid, inner core solid), lag (S falls about 12 s behind per 100 km), drill (deepest hole about 12 km), order (P about 6 km/s against S about 3.5 km/s).

readability.evidence: Kid text scores FK grade 2.9 and adult 7.4 by learn/readability.py, inside the learner limits of 6.5 and 9.5. Technical words (longitudinal, transverse, refraction) appear in the adult text with plain meanings in the kid text.

no_filler.evidence: Every paragraph carries a fact or a reason: the two waves, how each moves and why S stops in liquids, what the gap measures, and what the shadow zone proves; the adult text adds curriculum links, speeds, the discovery history with dates and the common mistakes without repeating the kid text.

mobile.evidence: At 390 px the canvas uses the tall ratio: the two wave bins sit side by side with their spring drawings, the pass test keeps its block and two large answer keys, the seismogram spans full width above the 0 to 500 km track, the cut-through Earth fits the width with its legend below, and the clue boxes stack in one column.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin: P wave and S wave, Gets through and Stopped, Closer, Further and Check this spot, one button per station angle (30° to 175°) and one per conclusion. say() updates the canvas aria-label and the polite live region after every action.
